title: Rightward and Downward Grapheme Distributions in the Voynich Manuscript
summary: Feaster studies relative positions within lines and paragraphs, concentrating on matched word forms differing by one grapheme. Three selected case studies show differences within line interiors as well as at their edges; the paper describes positional explanations as possibilities, not established readings.
established: Using paragraph text in Zandbergen–Landini version 1.7, the study defines relative rightwardness as zero-based position divided by line token count minus one. It resolves annotated ambiguity using the first non-question-mark option and omits uncertain-space commas (section 2).

For matched forms beginning Sh and ch, mean positions in the line interior are 0.433 and 0.481 respectively. Nineteen of 21 frequent matched pairs retain the direction when line-edge words are excluded (section 2, Table 1).

For matched forms beginning qo and o, interior mean positions are 0.487 and 0.517 respectively; for matched k and t forms they are 0.490 and 0.541. The paper selects these cases to illustrate patterns and does not present them as a prespecified exhaustive search (section 2, Tables 2–3).

The paper proposes positional distributions as one possible contributor to cross-word boundary frequencies and illustrates this using y.q and n.q; it leaves generalization to other boundary combinations open (section 5).

open.question: How do the reported line-interior positional differences vary with line length and manuscript section?
open.check: Prespecify the Sh/ch, qo/o and k/t contrasts, measure relative interior positions by line-length and section strata in independent transcriptions, and evaluate the fixed comparisons on held-out pages.

open.question: How much of the observed cross-word boundary frequency structure is explained by line and paragraph position beyond the illustrated y.q and n.q examples?
open.check: Use position-matched randomizations to compare a prespecified set of boundary pairs on public pages, and evaluate the fixed aggregate comparison on held-out pages.
